title: The bakery's website: ordering a cake
audience: The bakery owner, who takes cake orders by phone today
ask: Click through how a customer would order a cake on the website. Judge each step, then pick how people pay.
afterwards: Steps you agree with I build as shown; the rest I change and send back. Nothing goes online until you say so.

brief.question: Is this how you want people to order a cake from your website?
brief.explains: A small website: the cakes you make, one page per cake, and an order form with a pickup day. Orders reach you by email, and a day you are fully booked cannot be picked. Nothing is built yet: every page is a sketch.
brief.recommendation: Keep it to four pages and take payment at pickup at first. A website that only takes orders can be live in a week; online payment can come once people use it.
risks: Without a deposit, some people will order and not come. A reminder email the day before cuts that down; a deposit stops it.
The pickup days must match your real week. If the calendar is out of date, the website promises cakes you cannot make.

recommended.why: Nothing to set up and no fees: the website can go live this week. Add a deposit if people order and do not come.
